description: List defect/maintenance tickets, newest first (capped at ~500 — narrow with filters if truncated). Filter by itemId, statuses (open, in_progress, done, wontfix — "open tickets" usually means open + in_progress), type, or a text search over title and description. Use this to find the ticket your user means before update_ticket. Every row carries `createdAt` (when the problem was reported, which is what "newest first" sorts on and what answers "since when has this been broken?") and `reporterName` (who reported it; absent when nobody did — a maintenance plan minted the ticket, or it came from a logged-out QR report). Dates come twice: the epoch and its ISO twin — `createdAtIso` / `closedAtIso` as UTC instants, `dueAtIso` as a plain calendar day. Read the ISO one; this server does no timezone conversion, so do not re-zone a calendar day. Ask whether something was already reported by searching here before creating a second ticket for it. A ticket has no printed code and its `id` is a machine handle for your next call — when you name a ticket to your user, give them the `webUrl` link and the title, never the raw id. You see the same tickets the connected user sees in the app.
